focus: How skills/rust-anything/SKILL.md and whole-app.md steer a coding agent through a port
noveltyJustification: All 10 findings are new to this packet: 9 are confirmed absences in the sk-code Rust set (operating contract, stop gates, write-surface rule, port rules, failure-mode bans, stall detector, tolerance rule, session map, interview protocol) and 1 is partial (per-source-language traps).
keyQuestions: How do skills/rust-anything/SKILL.md and whole-app.md steer a coding agent through a port?
answeredQuestions: How do skills/rust-anything/SKILL.md and whole-app.md steer a coding agent through a port?
ruledOut: Reading docs/whole-apps.md in this iteration: skills/rust-anything/whole-app.md is the agent-facing steering document the question names and already carries the map, claim protocol and interview
Treating the stop gates as a conflict with sk-code's autonomous workflow doctrine: that doctrine governs sk-code's own loop, not a port against an external original

label: rust-anything's SKILL.md opens with an operating contract and a completion test ('rust-anything gives you ground truth; you write the Rust. Port one unit at a time, even when the goal is the whole app, and call a port done only when gate passes'); sk-code's SKILL.md is a reference map of six sections with no operating contract and no completion test.

rust-anything's skill is a numbered procedure with explicit stop gates ('Wait for the user's approval of the plan and of the first unit' at step 1, 'wait for their go-ahead before the next unit' at step 5); the sk-code Rust set has zero hits for ask the user, wait for, approval or go-ahead outside the checklist severity legend.

rust-anything's skill names the one file the agent may write and the command that regenerates the rest ('Write the port in src/port.rs only; src/lib.rs and the wrappers are generated. After changing a signature in port.rs, run rust-anything refresh'); the sk-code set has no write-surface rule separating generated from hand-written files.

rust-anything's skill reads port rules before writing and appends one the moment the user corrects behaviour, so the next unit and the next agent keep it; the sk-code set has zero hits for RULES.md, and this is the agent-facing half of the durable-correction gap.

rust-anything's skill carries a per-source-language trap list a general Rust standard would never contain: UTF-16 vs UTF-8 string offsets via src/utf16.rs, char::is_alphanumeric vs Java's Character.isLetterOrDigit and Python's str.isalpha, Python/Ruby int round-tripping via crate::pynum::Num, C crash: inputs as undefined behaviour, C pointer shapes, indexmap where order reaches output, fancy-regex for lookaround, and unicode(false) where the original's \w is ASCII-only; sk-code covers -0.0 and sort order but has no per-source-language trap list.

rust-anything's skill names the two agent failure modes and forbids them in one line each ('cargo test passing with no tests proves nothing: the recorded cases are the proof' and 'A mismatch is a behavior difference: fix the port, never the recording'); the sk-code set has no equivalent.

rust-anything's skill has a stall detector and a prescribed response: when diff reports trend.stalled (three changes to port.rs in a row gained no matching case), stop editing and show the user the remaining mismatches; the sk-code set has no stall rule.
rust-anything's skill forbids widening a float tolerance to make a mismatch go away ('a difference beyond it is a bug in the port'); the sk-code set has no float-tolerance rule at all.

whole-app.md is a session-spanning protocol built on a claimable map: rust/MAP.md carries the goal, the ADR index, every unit with its state (open, claimed by <session> <date>, done), open questions and out-of-scope items, a session claims one unit before starting and marks it done with its gate and replay results, and a new session starts by reading MAP.md then HANDOFF.md; the sk-code set has no multi-session protocol.

whole-app.md opens with a structured interview shaped as a design tree asked in rounds (a round is the whole frontier of decisions whose prerequisites are settled, each question numbered with a recommended answer worded so yes accepts it), seeded by shape, scope, equivalence bar, compatibility, dependencies, targets, checkpoints and cutover; the sk-code set has no interview protocol.

direction: Reading docs/whole-apps.md during the agent-steering iteration
reason: skills/rust-anything/whole-app.md is the agent-facing steering document the question names and already carries the map, the claim protocol and the interview.
